drafted_from: tool row in tools/gather-words-from-people/tool-rows.json, do-work/gather-words-on-the-records-door.mjs, read-data/gathered-words.mjs and test/gather-words.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Sam Example replied to my ask on list:praise: keep the words 'The cake was the best part of the day.' with consent first-name, because Sam wrote 'Replied: yes, first name is fine'." It runs tool:keep-the-words-a-person-gave on Sam's asked row and marks it received.

lists.label: Praise
lists.holds: One row per person asked for their own words about a case: the words, the consent they gave, the reason it was the time to ask and where the row stands (asked, received, approved, declined or withdrawn).

values.words: The cake was the best part of the day.
values.consent_note: Replied: yes, first name is fine

alike: the reviews list in a help desk
a Notion table of customer quotes

instructions: 1. Pour the two example rows into the testimonials list you already keep (see pour), or make list:praise from the ten fields above and give it a gathers block saying which field is which.
2. Ask first with tool:ask-people-for-words, or have words nobody asked for: give who instead of row_id.

3. Say what the person wrote, exactly, which of the list's consents they gave and their own words that gave it. The AI calls tools:run for tool:keep-the-words-a-person-gave with list, type, row_id (or who), words, consent and consent_note.
4. Read row_id, status (received) and changed. Changed words are reviewed again: approve them with tool:approve-words-to-show.

worked_examples.title: Keep Sam's reply on the row that asked
worked_examples.ask: Sam Example replied to my ask: keep their words with first-name consent.

worked_examples.given: From tools/gather-words-from-people/test/gather-words.test.mjs (keeping words records them with the consent given and the words that gave it, and marks the row received). list:praise must hold a gathers block (a bakery list shaped like the one in test/gather-words.test.mjs: consents full-name, first-name, no-name and private, anonymous heading 'A customer', ask subject 'How did the cake go, {name}?'). Sam's row is the asked row from the ask example (status asked).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"row_id":"record:praise:d9cbfc282b44d3c7c2029ca5d06c3c92","status":"received","changed":true} (the row now holds the words, consent first-name and the consent note; sending the same call again answers changed false; a consent not in the list is refused and the consent ids are named: full-name, first-name, no-name, private).

pour.how: Name the testimonials list you already keep and its fields. The tool matches each of the ten fields of list:praise to one of yours (the map you give, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), refuses when fewer than 80% match, and otherwise answers the records:write that adds the two example rows to your list. The list also needs its own gathers block (which field holds the words, the speaker, the consent and the state, the consents and what each state is called) before these tools take it.
